title: Bump opum-lore pin to lore-cli v0.7.0
summary: npm published lore-cli v0.7.0 (latest moved, confirmed independently on the main package and spot-checked platform packages). Lift the hold recorded in this repo's persistent memory (opum-lore-pin-held-at-v0.6.1.md) and bump the pin. Unlike v0.6.1 and v0.6.2, this IS a real content change -- LCLI-480 added ~13 lines to skills/lore/SKILL.md, moving skills/ from 24277e9a to 2998f74d -- so the baseline update carries actual new content, not just a ref move. Chain already independently verified in a prior session; this task re-confirms npm status and lands the change.

acceptanceCriteria.text: npm dist-tags.latest independently confirmed as 0.7.0 for @opum-ai/lore and spot-checked on platform packages, not taken from the publish/poll claim alone.

v0.7.0 skills/ tree resolved independently via the GitHub API chain (ref -> tag object -> commit -> root tree -> skills subtree) -- already done in a prior verification pass, confirmed as a REAL content change (2998f74d, not a re-tag over 24277e9a like the last two bumps).
plugin.json at v0.7.0 self-declares version 0.7.0, checked directly.
marketplace.json ref and federated-pin-baselines.json opum-lore entry (ref, trees.skills, verifiedAt, note) moved together to v0.7.0.
Both federated checker scripts and their regression suites pass locally against the new pin before landing.

implementationNotes:
AC1-3 verification, run independently rather than taken from lore-cli's poll.

AC1: `npm view @opum-ai/lore dist-tags --json` -> latest "0.7.0"; `npm view @opum-ai/lore version` -> "0.7.0". Spot-checked three platform packages given lore-cli's own note about registry-read propagation lag on this publish (up to 200s on some packages): @opum-ai/lore-darwin-arm64, @opum-ai/lore-linux-x64, @opum-ai/lore-win32-x64 all resolved 0.7.0 with no 404s. Confirms the registry has actually settled, not just that a publish command exited 0.

AC2: skills/ tree for v0.7.0 was independently resolved in a prior session on this same task chain, via the GitHub API (ref v0.7.0 -> tag object 9208d9c5 -> commit 5c437eb5 -> root tree 82f95781 -> skills subtree 2998f74d077845f8ad73f83aa296e37e034378a4), matching lore-cli's own numbers exactly. This is confirmed as a REAL content change -- unlike v0.6.1/v0.6.2 which were pure re-tags over an unchanged 24277e9a skills/ tree, this baseline value is actually moving.

AC3: fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opum-ai/lore-cli/v0.7.0/.claude-plugin/plugin.json directly in the prior verification pass -- version field reads "0.7.0", self-consistent.

Also worth recording: ran check-federated-content.mjs unmodified against the OLD pin (v0.6.2) before this bump and confirmed it still passed cleanly -- v0.7.0 being tagged never put the repo at risk, this bump is being made now because npm caught up, not because anything was broken.
references: lore-cli LCLI-469 (the release handshake protocol this task is fulfilling)
finalSummary: Lifted the hold: npm dist-tags.latest moved to 0.7.0 (confirmed independently on the main package and spot-checked on three platform packages given lore-cli's own note about registry propagation lag -- no 404s). Unlike v0.6.1 and v0.6.2, this is a real content bump: LCLI-480 added ~13 lines to skills/lore/SKILL.md, moving skills/ from 24277e9a to 2998f74d. That chain was independently resolved via the GitHub API in an earlier session (ref -> tag object -> commit -> root tree -> skills subtree, matching lore-cli's numbers exactly) and re-confirmed today when the content checker passed cleanly against the NEW pin and NEW baseline together, proving the recorded value actually matches the tag rather than just matching what I typed. plugin.json at the tag self-declares 0.7.0. Also verified before touching anything: check-federated-content.mjs run unmodified against the OLD pin (v0.6.2) still passed even after v0.7.0 was tagged elsewhere -- correcting lore-cli's initial claim that the check would go red on its own, which it can't, since it only re-resolves whatever ref is currently pinned. Moved marketplace.json's ref and the baseline entry together; both federated checkers and their regression suites pass locally (5/5, 8/8).
